conflicts.quote: A release that adds spreads without max loss should not ship.
conflicts.why: This and my §8 non-goal 2 (payoff math out of scope) cannot both stand. The disagreement is NOT feasibility — PM's assumption is correct: max loss, max gain and breakeven are computable client-side from the v3 leg set alone, with no backend call, no vendor data and no new dependency, and v3 deliberately stores everything they need (side, qty, multiplier, strike, right, expiration per leg). Two technical facts the owner should weigh before ruling. First: the expensive and dangerous part is not arithmetic on a defined-risk vertical, it is UNBOUNDED-case detection — an uncovered short call, a ratio with more short than long contracts, a short leg whose cover expires earlier than it does. An under-detected unbounded case renders a finite max loss on a genuinely unlimited position: a confidently wrong risk number, which is worse than no number and is the exact failure mode the honesty rules exist to prevent. Second: payoff math needs ZERO durable schema. It can ship in a follow-on with no migration and no re-work, whereas everything else in this feature is one irreversible union write across un-backed-up localStorage stores that hold the entire trading history. Sequencing payoff after the migration costs nothing durable; sequencing it inside doubles the blast radius of the one release that can lose history.
conflicts.proposal: Owner picks one. (a) This feature makes payoff math COMPUTABLE and a separate, immediately-following contract computes and displays it — PM's cut order (max gain, then breakeven, max loss never) transfers to that contract intact, and the BRIEF's decision-impact sentence is satisfied in two steps instead of one. (b) Payoff math lands here, effort is re-scoped above L, and numbers are emitted only on a WHITELIST of named single-expiration defined-risk shapes (verticals, iron condor, iron butterfly, covered call, protective put, collar); every uncovered-short, multi-expiration or Custom shape gets the stated reason instead of a computed figure. What must not happen either way is a generic max-loss function over an arbitrary leg set.

conflicts.why: The structure name is derived from the leg set and nothing else — PM's own §1(b) conservatism rests on that property. A cash-secured put and a naked short put have IDENTICAL leg sets: one short put leg, same strike, same expiration, same qty. The distinguishing fact is cash set aside as collateral, which is not a leg, is not in v3, and cannot be inferred: cash, collateral, buying power and account balance are non-goal 7, and this is a paper account with no cash model at all. So emitting the label Cash-secured put means asserting collateral the app has no record of, for every short put including one the trader has no cash behind. PM's own sentence concedes the mechanism (it is literally a short put) and then draws the opposite conclusion from it. Presenting one datum under two names, where the difference is a fact we do not hold, is what model-read-carries-its-assumptions forbids.
conflicts.proposal: The derived label is Short put. If the cash-secured framing has real product value it needs a STORED, opener-declared intent field on the position — which is a durable-schema-content decision that is cheap only while we are already migrating, so it is decided now or not at all. My default is drop it: it is a framing, not a fact, and covered call survives untouched because its cover IS a leg and therefore IS derivable.

conflicts.quote: Anything the classifier is not certain about
conflicts.why: structureKindOf is a total, pure function over a canonical leg signature: exact match against a named shape, else custom. It has no confidence, no score and no threshold, and it must not acquire one. A certainty framing invites a heuristic scorer, which makes the label non-deterministic across renders, makes custom a judgement rather than a residue, and destroys the property that carries the whole design — that a recognizer bug is cosmetic by construction because the label never feeds P/L, fills, persistence or any fetch. As written the criterion is not implementable; as implemented by a literal reader it is a fuzzy classifier inside a display-only path.
conflicts.proposal: Restate the Custom criterion as: any leg shape that is not an exact match for a structure in the named set renders Custom. Same product outcome, deterministic mechanism, and it preserves PM's asymmetry argument exactly. Separately and in PM's favour, I YIELD my §4 recognized set to PM's §1(b) named list: butterfly and non-iron condor come OUT of the derived enum and fall to custom, because removing a recognizer is as free as adding one and which names a trader sees is PM's call. R4 should write PM's list as the enum, plus custom, plus the Short put correction above.

conflicts.quote: **One short, dismissible, non-blocking notice** explaining what changed and pointing at export.
conflicts.why: I do not object to the notice; I object that AC-28 and AC-29 quietly add durable schema CONTENT that my R1 omitted, and durable content is the one thing this feature cannot revise cheaply afterwards. The union migration runs exactly once, and after the v3 promote-write the source blobs are never consulted again — that is the anti-resurrection rule and it is not negotiable, because a repeatedly-applied union resurrects records the trader has since closed or removed. Consequence: from the second load onward the app has no way to answer the question AC-28's only-clause and AC-29 both depend on, namely whether this trader had items in both places. Worse, a notice that exists only during the migrating render is gone forever if the trader reloads before reading it, and without a dismissal record it either reappears on every load or cannot be dismissed at all.
conflicts.proposal: The v3 blob carries a small non-record provenance block written in the SAME single promote-write: migrated_at, source_counts per source key, notice_dismissed. The notice fires if and only if both source counts are greater than zero; dismissal flips one boolean and touches no record; there is no second migration write path. The provenance block is never an input to P/L, grouping, the recognizer or the outcome ledger. If PM will accept a session-scoped notice instead, the durable fields drop out entirely — that is PM's call and I have put it in asks, because it must be answered before the schema is frozen, not after.

conflicts.why: Two corrections, one cosmetic and one that falsifies U2. Mechanism: the migration does not map Strategy values to StructureKind at all. It lifts a legacy record to a single leg, and the recognizer then derives the kind from the LEG; the old enum value is not carried forward anywhere, by design, which is what makes future recognizer changes migration-free. Substance: the guarantee cannot be given unconditionally. A source record with a missing or garbage right, an absent or zero qty, or a ghost-trade record that never held a full contract identity lifts to a leg matching no named shape, and it will render Custom. The lift is forbidden from fabricating a right or a strike to make the row name nicely — an invented instrument fact in an audit spine is strictly worse than a neutral Custom chip, and the same lift function is reused by the archive import, so any fabrication would also silently rewrite an imported backup.
conflicts.proposal: Weaken U2 to: a WELL-FORMED migrated single-leg option position renders exactly as shipped (long call, long put, short call, short put), and its P/L figure is bit-identical before and after. Treat Custom on a migrated row as a rare but legitimate outcome for a malformed legacy record, not a defect. UX already owns copy that makes this harmless, since Custom is neutral by design. This matters because U2 as written is falsified by a single corrupt legacy record and would then be reported at GATE Q as a migration bug when it is the migration behaving correctly.

conflicts.quote:
2. **Payoff math**: breakeven, max profit, max loss, margin, buying power, assignment/exercise, early
   assignment on short legs.
conflicts.why: This deletes the feature's stated reason for existing. The BRIEF's Decision impact is explicit: a debit spread's real breakeven and max loss are currently uncomputable, so the app cannot tell the trader what they actually risk. Made-computable is not an observable outcome — a trader cannot see a data model. My AC-14/15/16 and UX's own §6 slot both assume at least max loss lands; with this non-goal standing, the ONLY new user-visible outcome of an L-effort release is a row that says `Iron condor` instead of two rows. I am not narrowing scope silently to fit the non-goal, and I am not asking the architect to absorb payoff math without an effort re-estimate — this is exactly the priority call the owner is entitled to make.
conflicts.proposal: Owner picks one of three, explicitly: (a) max loss ONLY for named single-expiration defined-risk structures in v1 — verticals, iron condors, iron butterflies — with `Unlimited` where the worst case is unbounded and a stated reason everywhere else; max gain and breakeven deferred. This is my cut order from R1 §2 and the smallest thing that satisfies the BRIEF. (b) All three figures, and the effort goes from L to L+ with payoff math contracted separately. (c) None of it in this feature, in which case the BRIEF's Decision impact sentence must be rewritten before GATE C closes and I will drop AC-14/15/16 and tell UX to cut its §6 Max loss slot — but the owner should know they are shipping the representation and not the answer.

conflicts.why: Which shapes get a name is a product call and this set contradicts mine in both directions. It NAMES `butterfly` and `condor` (non-iron), which my R1 §1(b) deliberately routes to Custom — a mislabelled 1x2 or a non-iron condor is the dangerous direction, because the trader sizes off the name. And it DROPS names I asked for that a Webull account is full of: protective put, collar, iron butterfly, cash-secured put. By the architect's own §4 the label is display-only and adding a recognizer later is a pure function change with zero migration, so nothing technical rides on this — which is precisely why the set should be mine and not a side effect of enum design.
conflicts.proposal: Adopt the R1 §1(b) named list as the v1 recognizer set: add `protective_put`, `collar`, `iron_butterfly`, and either `cash_secured_put` or an explicit decision that a short put is labelled `Short put` only (see my ask below); drop `butterfly` and `condor` from v1 recognition so those shapes render `Custom · N legs` until we see them arrive. Everything else in the architect's set stands unchanged. If a recognizer is cheaper to write than to omit, keep the code and gate the LABEL — but the trader must not see a name we are not confident in.

conflicts.quote:
3. With the promote aborted, the store runs **in-memory** from whatever did parse, and **every
   durable write is REFUSED**, visibly (the mutator returns false; the caller surfaces it).
conflicts.why: I accept never-overwrite — it is the right rule and my AC-31 depends on it. What cannot stand is shipping this as an internal boolean. As written, a trader with one unreadable legacy blob enters a mode where the app looks normal, accepts an entry, and then that position is gone on reload. That is a whole product state — Convexa has become read-only — and it exists in neither my ACs nor UX's twenty component states. `the caller surfaces it` is the entire user-facing design of a mode in which nothing the trader does persists, and it silently converts a data-protection decision into a decision to stop the trader trading.
conflicts.proposal: Make the faulted mode a first-class, specified product state before it is built: a persistent (not dismissible) banner stating that saved data could not be read, that NOTHING was deleted, that new positions will not be saved until it is resolved, and offering export; entry affordances visibly disabled rather than accepting input and failing after the fact. Owner call inside that: whether refusing ALL durable writes is the behaviour we want, or whether new positions may be accepted into a fresh store while the unreadable blob is left untouched. I lean to the architect's stricter rule, but a trader locked out of recording a live trade is a consequence the owner should choose, not inherit.

conflicts.quote: `position_eval` therefore becomes an approximation for multi-leg.
conflicts.why: Stated where? The statement lives in a pure FE function, not in the trader's view. A trader holding a four-leg condor would get a position-context assessment computed from one long leg, rendered in exactly the same surface and voice as an assessment of a single long call. That is the app becoming confidently wrong about the structures this feature exists to introduce, and it is `model-read-carries-its-assumptions` broken at the read that matters most. I am not asking for a backend change — the empty `apps/api` diff holds either way. I am refusing to let an approximation ship undisclosed because disclosure was assumed to be somebody else's line item.
conflicts.proposal: Owner picks: (a) the alert/assessment still fires for multi-leg but carries a visible qualifier naming the leg it evaluated (e.g. assessed on the $400 call leg only), or (b) the position-context assessment is suppressed for any position with more than one leg and says so, rather than answering about a leg while appearing to answer about the position. Either way it needs an AC and UX copy. What must not happen is (c): the same UI, the same confidence, one leg of four.

conflicts.quote:
**Group axis becomes `None · Ticker · Structure · Expiry`** (Expiry returns to the toolbar; it was
dropped at REVISION 2 and multi-expiry positions make it meaningful again).
conflicts.why: REVISION 2 removed that control deliberately. Re-adding a previously-removed toolbar axis is new scope and a reversal of a shipped owner decision, and it is arriving inside a feature whose risk surface is a durable migration. My R1 scope says grouping/filtering/sorting/saved views continue to work over the new shape — continue, not grow. UX's own reasoning (calendars need a group axis) is sound, which is exactly why it should be an owner decision rather than a UX judgement call folded into a refactor.
conflicts.proposal: Route to the owner as a yes/no: restore Group-by-Expiry now because multi-expiry structures make it meaningful, or hold it as a Future item and let calendars group under Structure in v1 (in which case UX cuts U17 as its position already offers). If it is held, nothing else in the UX position changes. I have no objection to the axis on its merits — only to it landing unremarked.

conflicts.quote:
The BRIEF's "a debit spread's real breakeven
   is uncomputable" is fixed here in the sense of **made computable**, not computed.
conflicts.why: This is head-on with PM §2, which lists max loss as product-required and says "**Max loss is not cuttable.**" plus AC-14/AC-15/AC-16/AC-17. The two positions cannot both be executed. My lane cannot absorb the difference: PM's AC-16 requires "the at-expiration figures are replaced by a short stated reason — never blank, never `0`", and a *replacement* reason is uninstantiable copy if the figures never exist — there is nothing to replace, and I would be writing a sentence explaining the absence of a feature rather than the limits of a number. It also decides whether §4's design direction has a fourth read on the row ("what can I lose") or three. I am not asking to settle it in my lane; I am refusing to write both copy sets and let GATE Q pick.
conflicts.proposal: Owner picks one of: (a) payoff math IN — max loss only for named single-expiration defined-risk structures, with breakeven/max gain deferred, per PM's own cut order; I then own the withheld-reason copy and the `Unlimited` wording; or (b) payoff math OUT — PM drops AC-14/15/16/17 to Future and the BRIEF's decision-impact sentence is explicitly restated as "made computable", so nobody discovers at GATE Q that the stated reason for the feature did not ship. Not (c): ship a half-set where max loss appears for some structures and no reason appears for the rest.

conflicts.why: I own the closed `STRUCTURE_LABEL` lookup, and this enum cannot carry the labels PM's §1(b) requires — in both directions. Under-names: PM's named set asks for "Call debit spread", "Put credit spread", Protective put, Collar, Cash-secured put and Iron butterfly; `vertical_debit`/`vertical_credit` carry no call/put discriminator, so one enum member has to render two different trader-facing names, which is exactly the mis-labeling PM's risk 4 is about. Over-names: this set contains `butterfly` and `condor` (non-iron), which PM explicitly assigns to Custom ("Call butterfly / put butterfly (non-iron)", "Non-iron condors"). A closed lookup whose domain neither matches nor is a subset of the product's named set is not a lookup — it is a second, silent naming decision made in a pure module. This invalidates my U2 and PM's AC-8 simultaneously.
conflicts.proposal: One enum, one owner: PM's §1(b) table is the domain, the architect's `structureKindOf` is the recognizer over it, and the enum gains whatever discriminator the labels need (either four vertical members or a `right` field on the view row) so no member maps to two names. Any shape PM assigns to Custom is *not* a recognizer member in v1 — adding it later is the free change the architect already argues for. I write one label per member and `Custom · N legs` for the rest; I will not write a label that hedges across two structures.

conflicts.quote:
And the **`pl_pct_basis` discriminator rides with the
number** because percent-of-net-credit is a genuinely different quantity from percent-of-net-debit
and presenting both as "P/L %" without a basis is exactly what `[model-read-carries-its-assumptions]`
forbids.
conflicts.why: I accept the honesty argument and cannot render it as stated. "Rides with the number" in a fixed-width dense table cell means either a suffix (`+18% of net credit` blows the `nowrap` mono cell and is the documented 393px overflow mechanism) or a new column, and my R1 binds "I am adding **no new column** in this feature." There is a second, sharper consequence the architect's `null` percent creates in my lane: `—` already carries two meanings on this surface (not-applicable, and pending-limit), and my U8 binds that two different truths never share one glyph. A third meaning — "percent is undefined because net cost is ~0" — lands on the same em dash and silently breaks the one distinction I flagged as most likely to regress quietly.
conflicts.proposal: Disclosure without a column: the `pl_pct` cell renders the number bare, the **column header** carries the basis-aware tooltip, and the cell's own tip names the basis for that row ("+18% — measured against the $115 net credit you received, not against capital at risk"). For `pl_pct === null` the cell renders the literal word `undefined`, not `—`, with its own tip. If the architect judges a tooltip insufficient for `[model-read-carries-its-assumptions]` on a number this load-bearing, the honest alternative is not a suffix — it is that P/L% for credit structures is withheld in v1, which is a product call, not mine.

conflicts.quote:
With the promote aborted, the store runs **in-memory** from whatever did parse, and **every
   durable write is REFUSED**, visibly (the mutator returns false; the caller surfaces it).
conflicts.why: "The caller surfaces it" hands my lane the most dangerous state in the feature with no design and no copy, and a boolean return is the exact shape that gets ignored at the call site. Nothing in my R1, PM's ACs, or this position names what the trader sees while writes are refused. Unspecified, it renders as: the trader opens a position, the dialog closes, the row appears (in-memory), and it is gone on reload — a silent data loss produced by the code path whose whole purpose is preventing silent data loss. PM's AC-31 covers the *read* side ("an honest message stating that nothing was deleted") but says nothing about the app continuing to accept writes it will not keep.
conflicts.proposal: Name it as a first-class component state — `store-faulted` — with three properties, all mine to word: (1) a persistent, **non-dismissible** banner above the table, warning-class WITH an icon per canon, saying we could not read your saved positions, nothing was deleted, and new positions will not be saved until this is fixed; (2) the entry CTA **disabled** with that reason in its tooltip, not enabled-then-failing; (3) Close and every other mutator disabled the same way. That requires the store to expose a *faulted* flag to the view layer, not just a `false` return per call — an architecture change I am asking for, not making.

conflicts.quote: `position_eval` therefore becomes an approximation for multi-leg.
conflicts.why: I do not contest the approximation; I contest that it can stay unstated in the read. The Ticker-page position-context alert addresses the trader about "your position" while being computed from one leg of four, and under canon rule 4 / `[model-read-carries-its-assumptions]` a model read that names the wrong subject is overclaiming — the same class as the tinted hit-rate. Worse is the other branch: "none if the structure has no option leg" means a shares-only position produces *no* alert at all, and a silent absence is indistinguishable from "nothing changed", which is the failure mode this app is built against. Neither state has copy in any of the three positions.
conflicts.proposal: Two strings, both mine to write once the seam exists: any position-context alert on a multi-leg structure names the leg it evaluated ("Based on the $400 call leg — Convexa evaluates one leg of a multi-leg position"), and a position with no option leg renders an explicit stated non-evaluation rather than silence. The architect's side of it is that the primary-leg selection must be *readable* from `PositionView` (which leg won), not an anonymous internal choice.

conflicts.quote: **Withheld risk figures get a visible short reason in place of the number**, and the space to say it.
conflicts.why: This is an assumption about my lane I cannot honor as written at 393px, and it is the second-order cost of §2 that the cut order does not price. My R1 caps the mobile card footer at exactly four items (`Qty` · net debit/credit · `Mark` · expiry) because that is what fits without horizontal overflow — a shipped, e2e-enforced constraint. Max loss + max gain + breakeven is three more figures; a *stated reason* in place of each is three more sentences. Both cannot sit on a collapsed 393px card, and putting them there is precisely how `scrollWidth 580 vs 393` happened before. The row is a scan surface, not a risk report.
conflicts.proposal: Contingent on the payoff-math conflict resolving IN: the collapsed row/card carries at most **one** risk figure (max loss, the uncuttable one), and max gain + breakeven + all withheld-reason copy live in the leg disclosure, which is already the designed home for per-position detail and has vertical room for a sentence. If PM requires all three visible on the collapsed row at 393px, that is a different card — its own design pass, and it costs the density this surface exists for. Owner priority call, not a UX preference.

conflicts.quote:
This is the
   number the trader typed and the number their broker showed them.
conflicts.why: The architect's schema makes this false in a way that changes what the entry form asks for: `entry_price` is stored **per leg**, positive, and `netEntryCost` is a SUM — so the net is *derived*, not typed. Only one of two designs is possible and they are not equivalent. If the trader types per-leg prices, the net is computed and my shipped dialog copy `— user-entered, not a market quote` is a claim about the legs, not the net. If the trader types a net (which is what their broker actually quotes them, per this sentence), per-leg entry prices must be back-solved and written into the durable record — fabricated per-leg facts in the same audit spine where the architect refuses to backfill an invented `entry_time`. I will not write copy that presents a fabricated per-leg price as the trader's own number.
conflicts.proposal: Per-leg entry prices are typed; the net is computed and **labeled as computed** in the dialog (`Net debit $840 · computed from your leg prices`), and the position row's net entry carries the same provenance in its tip. If PM insists the trader types the net because that is what the broker shows, the architect needs to answer whether an allocated per-leg price can be stored honestly (e.g. flagged as allocated) — a schema conversation, not a copy one.

conflicts.quote: **I am binding: no call/put tint in positions.** This is a deliberate divergence from a literal reading of `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`'s palette-role column and I want it argued in R2, not discovered at GATE Q
conflicts.why: Raising my own R1 as a conflict because it is a divergence from the design canon of record and neither sibling position touches it, so it would otherwise pass unratified. `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` lines 42-43 state `success` is "**RESERVED** — calls / +gamma / +P&L direction" and `error` "**RESERVED** — puts / −gamma / −P&L direction", which literally permits a green `Call` and a red `Put` in my leg list. The `convexa-design` skill's rule 2 says green/red are reserved for *direction* of P/L or flow, and a call is not a direction. On this surface the literal reading produces a green `Call` label one cell from a red P/L on the same losing row — the proximity-chip regression, exactly. Two owner-owned documents disagree, and the skill's "where they conflict, this skill wins" clause is written about the generic skills, not about `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`, so I cannot settle it myself.
conflicts.proposal: Ratify the divergence as **scoped, not global**: green/red keep the calls/puts role in the GEX-chart domain where they encode flow direction, and are banned on any leg attribute (`Call`/`Put`, `Long`/`Short`, `debit`/`credit`) on the positions surface, where the only direction present is P/L. If ratified, `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`'s palette-role column gains "(GEX domain)" so the next reader does not rediscover this, and the className-identity guard in my U15 enforces it. If rejected, U15 changes and I need to know now, because it is a `test`-class AC.
